title: Getting started
text: Getting started HypeDE is a Chrome OS–style desktop that runs on top of an unmodified GNOME Shell. It installs as a separate session: your regular GNOME stays as it was, and HypeDE keeps its own settings.

title: Getting started
text: Install Arch Linux, CachyOS and other Arch-based systems with GNOME Shell 48–50: git clone https://github.com/hypede/hypede cd hypede/packaging makepkg -si KDE modules for Settings are optional. Without one, its row in Settings names the package to install: sudo pacman -S plasma-nm bluedevil plasma-pa print-manager plasma-workspace \ plasma-desktop kde-cli-tools flatpak-kcm kinfocenter power-profiles-daemon The AI assistant needs webkitgtk-6.0 . Other distributions: make && sudo make install , see the README for dependencies.

title: Getting started
text: First sign-in Log out and pick HypeDE on the login screen (GDM, SDDM, greetd and LightDM all show it). HypeDE copies your keyboard layouts, mouse, touchpad, accessibility and shortcut settings from GNOME. A short greeting appears; turn it off in Settings → Personalization → Animations and effects .

title: Getting started

title: Shelf and launcher
text: The shelf The shelf holds GNOME's own indicators, so everything that shows up in GNOME's top bar works here. Position : bottom, left, right or top — Settings → Shelf and launcher . Style : across the whole edge or floating, with its own size, icon size, opacity and blur. Apps : drag icons to reorder, right-click to pin or unpin. A dot shows running apps; clicking an app with several windows cycles through them. Auto-hide hides the shelf under maximised windows.

title: Shelf and launcher
text: The launcher Press Super or click the circle. Start typing to search: apps , settings and files in your home folder; sums — 12*(3+4) , 2^10 , 200*15% ; the web — anything else goes to your search engine; recent files appear under “Continue where you left off”. Choose what it searches and the search engine in Settings → Shelf and launcher . The launcher comes as a bubble or full screen.

title: Shelf and launcher
text: Commands Type a command and press Enter . Russian words work too. You type What happens dark , light switch dark style dnd , do not disturb Do Not Disturb on or off night light Night Light on or off wifi , bluetooth turn the radio on or off volume 40 set volume to 40 % brightness 70 set screen brightness timer 5 , timer 30 sec , timer 1 h a timer that rings when done coffee 30 keep the screen on for 30 minutes lock , screenshot lock the screen, take a screenshot sleep , log out , restart , shut down power actions empty trash empty the trash mode , mode game turn a focus mode on or off save session , restore session save or reopen your windows

title: Shelf and launcher
text: Asking the AI When the assistant is on, an Ask Claude button (named after your provider) appears next to the search results: it sends what you typed to the assistant.

title: Keys and gestures
text: Keys and gestures

title: Keys and gestures
text: Keyboard Shortcut Action Super open or close the launcher Super + S window overview Super + L lock the screen Super + 1 … 9 open the n-th app on the shelf Super + Space next keyboard layout Super + V clipboard history Super + Z float the window: small, on top of others; again to put it back Super + Shift + T reopen the window you just closed, in the same place Super + A ask the AI about the selected text Print Screen screenshot All of them can be changed in Settings → Device → Keyboard shortcuts . What Super opens (launcher or overview) is in Settings → Shelf and launcher .

title: Keys and gestures
text: Touchpad Gesture Action Four fingers up open the launcher — or bring back windows hidden by the gesture below Four fingers down show the desktop: windows slide away and minimise Three fingers up window overview (GNOME) Three fingers left or right switch desks (GNOME) Gestures follow your fingers one-to-one. Let go before about a third of the way and everything goes back. Four-finger gestures can be switched off in Settings → Device → Touchpad .

title: Keys and gestures
text: Mouse Drag a window to a screen edge to snap it to half the screen, to the top to maximise. Right-click an app on the shelf for its windows and actions. Right-click a desktop widget to add, move back or remove widgets.

title: Windows
text: Windows

title: Windows
text: Title bar buttons Minimise, maximise and close are shown for GTK 3, GTK 4 and libadwaita apps. Qt apps get GNOME-style title bars with qadwaitadecorations-qt6 (AUR). Change the buttons in Settings → Personalization → Windows . If an app still shows only a close button, see Troubleshooting .

title: Windows
text: Effects Effect What it does Switch Soft animations windows grow in with a slight spring and fade out Window animations Genie minimise the window flows into its shelf icon Genie minimize Jelly windows the window bends a little while you drag it and springs back Jelly windows Rounded corners for apps that draw square corners without a shadow Rounded window corners All are in Settings → Personalization → Animations and effects . Lite mode turns off blur and the heavier effects on slower computers.

title: Windows
text: Useful tricks Super + Z floats a window: it becomes small and stays above the others — handy for a video or a calculator. Super + Shift + T reopens the last ten closed windows, newest first.

title: Windows
text: Session restore HypeDE remembers which windows are open, on which desk, where and how big. At sign-in it offers to reopen them. Choose Ask , Always or Never in Settings → System preferences → Session . You can also type save session or restore session in the launcher. Apps reopen as new windows: documents inside them are restored only if the app itself does that.

title: Desktop
text: Desktop

title: Desktop
text: Icons Files from your Desktop folder appear on the desktop, plus Home and Trash if you like. Drag them into apps and back, double-click to open, right-click for the menu. Settings: Personalization → Desktop .

title: Desktop
text: Live wallpapers Personalization → Live wallpaper has animated wallpapers (waves, bokeh, gradient) and Video or GIF… for a file of your own. They pause when maximised windows cover the desktop, to save battery. Speed is adjustable; Lite mode turns them off.

title: Desktop
text: Widgets Widget Shows Clock time and date Calendar the month; arrows switch months Weather temperature and sky for the city chosen in GNOME Weather; click to open it System processor, memory and battery Music the song that is playing, with back, play and next; hidden when nothing plays Note a plain text note, saved as you type Add or remove in Personalization → Widgets , or right-click any widget. Move : drag a widget anywhere; it snaps to an 8-pixel grid. Return to the column puts it back on the right edge. Widgets live under windows, like icons. Show the desktop with four fingers down to see them.

title: Focus modes
text: Focus modes A focus mode switches several things at once and puts them back when you turn it off. Mode By default Work Do Not Disturb, balanced power Game Do Not Disturb, performance power, opens Steam if installed Study Do Not Disturb, balanced power, Lagoon theme

title: Focus modes
text: Turning a mode on the Focus tile in quick settings — its arrow lists the modes; or type mode , mode game in the launcher.

title: Focus modes
text: Editing modes Settings → System preferences → Focus modes . For each mode: name, Do Not Disturb, power mode, theme and apps to open. Add your own with New focus mode .

title: Focus modes
text: What gets restored When a mode turns off, HypeDE restores Do Not Disturb, the power profile and the whole look as it was before (the previous theme is saved to ~/.local/state/hypede/ ). Apps the mode opened stay open.

title: Themes and the theme store
text: Themes and the theme store A theme sets the whole look in one click: colours, wallpaper, shelf, launcher, windows, lock screen, fonts, icons and sounds. Everything is in Settings → Personalization .

title: Themes and the theme store
text: Using themes Apply : click a theme under Themes . Save your look : Save current look as a theme . Your own wallpapers are copied next to it. Export : Export current look writes a .json file with your wallpapers packed inside — send it to anyone. Import adds such a file to your themes. Delete : hover over your own theme and click the bin.

title: Themes and the theme store
text: The theme store Theme store lists themes published on GitHub. Install downloads, checks and applies a theme; it then appears among your themes. Reviewed by HypeDE means a maintainer looked at that exact version; Not reviewed yet themes passed the automatic checks only. You can also paste any repository link into the field under the store and press Install .

title: Themes and the theme store
text: Publishing your theme Set up the look you want and choose Export current look . Create a public GitHub repository and put the file in its root as theme.json . Optionally add preview.png — a 16:9 screenshot, up to 4 MB. In Theme store , paste the repository link and press Publish . HypeDE checks the repository and opens a ready request on GitHub. Submit it: within a minute a bot checks the theme again, adds it to the store and closes the request. The store keeps the exact commit it checked. To publish changes, push them and open a new request ( Publish again): the bot moves the store to your new commit.

title: Themes and the theme store
text: What is checked A theme is data, never code, and HypeDE treats every downloaded theme as untrusted: only appearance settings from a fixed list are applied, each checked by type and allowed range; a picture must really be the format its name says; it is decoded and re-encoded in a separate process with memory and time limits, so only the pixels survive; SVG files may not contain scripts, event handlers, external links, entities or embedded files; videos must be MP4, WebM, MKV or MOV and are probed before use; files are limited to 64 MB; if ClamAV is installed, every file is scanned with it; a downloaded theme may use wallpapers only from system folders and its own folder; the store pins each theme to a commit, so an author cannot silently change a published theme.

title: Themes and the theme store
text: File format A theme is a JSON file with "hypede-theme": 1 , a name and any of these groups: Group Fields colors scheme ( default , prefer-dark ), accent ( #rrggbb ), gnome-accent , shelf , menus wallpaper light , dark , fit , color , live , live-speed shelf position , alignment , style , size , icon-size , opacity , blur , indicator , hover-zoom , show-date launcher style , columns , icon-size , labels , opacity , blur desktop icons , icon-size , show-home , show-trash windows corner-radius , rounded-windows , window-radius , animations , animation-speed , genie , jelly , buttons , notifications , greeting lockscreen style , clock , clock-color , clock-size , message , wallpaper , blur , dim , waves , cards fonts interface , documents , monospace icons theme , cursor , cursor-size sounds theme Wallpapers are file:///usr/share/… paths or embedded:NAME pointing into a files object of base64-encoded pictures. Example: { "hypede-theme": 1, "name": "Deep Forest", "author": "you", "description": "Moss green on dark pine.", "colors": { "scheme": "prefer-dark", "gnome-accent": "green", "accent": "#9bd77c", "shelf": "#0e1a12", "menus": "#132219" }, "wallpaper": { "light": "file:///usr/share/hypede/wallpapers/forest.svg", "dark": "file:///usr/share/hypede/wallpapers/forest.svg" }, "shelf": { "style": "floating", "opacity": 82 }, "windows": { "corner-radius": 20, "genie": true } } From a terminal: hypede-theme list , apply , save , export , import , install , check .

title: AI assistant
text: AI assistant The assistant opens as a panel on the right edge of the screen, like on a Chromebook.

title: AI assistant
text: Setting it up Settings → AI assistant → turn it on. Pick a provider: Claude, Gemini, Mistral, ChatGPT, Grok or DeepSeek. Sign in opens the provider's own page: you use your own account. HypeDE never sees or stores your password and uses no API keys.

title: AI assistant
text: Where to ask the Ask Claude button (named after your provider) in the launcher sends what you typed; Super + A sends the selected text from any app; in Files, Ask sends the selected files; Ask Claude (or your provider) in the title bar of Settings asks about a setting.

title: AI assistant
text: Privacy The assistant only chats. It cannot run commands, change settings or read files on its own; it sees only what you send it. It is off until you turn it on.

title: Settings
text: Settings One window for everything, laid out like Chrome OS: search at the top, pages on the left. Page What is there Network, Bluetooth KDE modules ( plasma-nm , bluedevil ), proxy Device displays, mouse, touchpad, keyboard and shortcuts, sound and printers, power, storage Personalization themes, theme store, wallpaper, live wallpaper, desktop, widgets, style, animations Shelf and launcher position, style, size, what the launcher searches Lock screen clock style, colours, waves, cards, wallpaper, message Security and privacy history of recent files, protection Apps installed apps, default apps, notifications AI assistant provider and sign-in Accessibility text size, contrast, zoom, screen reader System preferences date and time, languages, boot splash, hardware, accounts, GNOME services, focus modes, session, startup apps, HypeDE configuration

title: Settings
text: Search Type in the search field at the top: it finds pages and individual settings, in English and Russian.

title: Settings
text: Backup System preferences → HypeDE configuration saves all HypeDE settings to a file and restores them. HypeDE's settings live in their own database, ~/.config/dconf/hypede , separate from regular GNOME.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Troubleshooting

title: Troubleshooting
section: An app shows only a close button
text: An app shows only a close button HypeDE writes the button layout for GTK 3, GTK 4 and libadwaita apps at sign-in. If one still shows only ×: sign out and back in once after installing or updating HypeDE; check Settings → Personalization → Windows → Window buttons ; restart Flatpak apps after changing the layout; Qt apps need qadwaitadecorations-qt6 for GNOME-style title bars.

title: Troubleshooting
text: The desktop feels slow turn on Lite mode in Personalization → Animations and effects : no blur, live wallpapers, rounded-corner effect or lock screen waves; turn off live wallpaper, or keep Pause under maximized windows on; lower Animation speed or switch off Genie minimize and Jelly windows .

title: Troubleshooting
text: A setting does nothing HypeDE keeps its own settings database. Running gsettings from a terminal outside the HypeDE session changes regular GNOME, not HypeDE. Inside a HypeDE session it works as expected.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Start from scratch Reset all HypeDE settings (regular GNOME is untouched), then sign out and back in: DCONF_PROFILE=hypede dconf reset -f /

title: Troubleshooting
text: The theme store is empty The store loads from GitHub. Without a connection Settings shows the last list it saw. Press Refresh once you are online.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Logs journalctl --user -b | grep -i -E "hypede|gnome-shell" Attach the relevant lines when you report a problem .

title: For developers
text: Build from source git clone https://github.com/hypede/hypede cd hypede make && sudo make install make install-user installs only the shell extension into ~/.local for use in regular GNOME.

title: For developers
text: Layout shell/extension/ shell: shelf, launcher, widgets, window effects, gestures, lock screen shell/theme/ stylesheet template (tools/gen-shell-css.py writes light and dark) session/ session startup, systemd units, password check apps/settings/ Settings (C++, QML, KCMUtils) apps/files/ Files (Python, GTK 4) apps/assistant/ AI assistant (Python, WebKitGTK) apps/theme/ hypede-theme: themes, store, file checks store/ theme store catalogue and built-in store themes data/ schemas, icons, sounds, wallpapers, themes tools/ generators, translations, dev scripts

title: For developers
section: Running the shell without a session
text: Running the shell without a session tools/dev/shell-headless.sh start 1600x900 runs a nested headless GNOME Shell with HypeDE; eval runs JavaScript in it, shot FILE takes a screenshot.

title: For developers
text: Translations English is the source. Russian strings live in tools/i18n/settings_ru.py (Settings) and tools/i18n/po_ru.py (shell). make pot regenerates po/ .

title: For developers
text: Tests python3 -m unittest discover -s apps/theme/tests -t apps/theme

title: For developers
text: Contributing Pull requests and issues are welcome on GitHub . Themes go through the theme store , not pull requests.
